proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOE restart Yucca Mountain licensing with the NRC, reconstitute the Office of Civilian Radioactive Waste Management and its director post under the Nuclear Waste Policy Act, and use consent-based siting to find a second repository or temporary sites. It also recommends new Nuclear Waste Fund mechanisms and market reforms that increase private-sector responsibility for waste, and more low-level waste facilities.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 the administration is pursuing a different waste strategy from the one the Mandate describes, and no restart of Yucca Mountain licensing was found. On 2026-01-28 DOE issued a request for information inviting states to express interest in hosting Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses, voluntary federal-state partnerships that could co-locate fuel fabrication, enrichment, used-fuel reprocessing and waste disposition; the release does not mention Yucca Mountain, the Nuclear Waste Policy Act or the Nuclear Waste Fund. DOE received 28 applications from 26 states by the 2026-04-01 deadline, and in July 2026 DOE named Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana and Idaho as initial contenders and signed non-binding memoranda of understanding with them (DOE's pages give 2026-07-24 and 2026-07-28 for the announcement); West Virginia signed one in September 2026. An AIP report of 2026-09-29 says DOE asked Congress to end Yucca Mountain's exclusive disposal role, authorize host-state agreements and interim storage, and make reprocessing policy where feasible, and that lawmakers in September hearings questioned using the Nuclear Waste Fund for recycling and raised concerns about DOE staffing; no DOE document containing that request was found. On 2026-02-25 the NRC discontinued a 2007-era security rulemaking for the Yucca repository, citing shifted priorities under Executive Order 14300, and said nothing about the licensing proceeding. On low-level waste, the NRC proposed a new disposal framework on 2026-07-01 (comments closed 2026-08-17). No reconstitution of OCRWM or Nuclear Waste Fund reform was found.

timeline.event: DOE issues a request for information inviting states to express interest in hosting Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses, voluntary federal-state partnerships that may include fuel fabrication, enrichment, used-fuel reprocessing and waste disposition (responses due 2026-04-01); the release does not mention Yucca Mountain, the Nuclear Waste Policy Act or the Nuclear Waste Fund. Nevada Current reported the announcement on 2026-02-03, with Nevada's nuclear projects commission chair saying it shows Yucca Mountain is not viable and noting a different permanent site would require changing the law.

NRC publishes a notice discontinuing three rulemakings, including a 2007 proposal on security requirements for the Yucca Mountain geologic repository operations area, citing a shift in priorities tied to Executive Order 14300 and the time elapsed; the notice does not address the status of the Yucca licensing proceeding.

NRC proposes a risk-informed framework for low-level radioactive waste disposal that adds some transuranic waste and higher-concentration waste, with comments due 2026-08-17; it states that it does not change legal requirements for geologic disposal of high-level waste or spent fuel.

DOE names Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana and Idaho as initial contenders to host Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses and signs non-binding memoranda of understanding with each, after receiving 28 applications from 26 states; hosting agreements would follow later. DOE's campus page gives a press release date of 2026-07-24 and says West Virginia signed a memorandum in September 2026. The pages do not mention Yucca Mountain or request legislation.

AIP FYI reports that DOE asked Congress for new authority to end Yucca Mountain's exclusive legal status as the disposal site, negotiate host-state agreements, authorize interim storage at campus sites and make reprocessing policy where feasible; 26 states responded to DOE's request for interest and six signed non-binding memorandums of understanding. At September hearings, House Energy and Commerce leaders urged caution about using the Nuclear Waste Fund for recycling, and utility regulators and the Nuclear Energy Institute said the fund should be reserved for disposal.

title: Restart Yucca Mountain licensing, reconstitute OCRWM, and raise industry role in waste
uncertainties: DOE's request to Congress to end Yucca Mountain's exclusive status still rests on one AIP report: DOE's campus pages (read through fetch summaries) do not mention Yucca Mountain or legislation, and no DOE legislative proposal or testimony was found (searches for a legislative proposal and the September 2026 hearing returned only older items and a Bloomberg Government piece of 2026-04-16 saying Secretary Wright expects to work with Congress on updating the Nuclear Waste Policy Act). DOE's pages give two dates for the July 2026 announcement (2026-07-24 on the program page, 2026-07-28 on the contenders article) and the program page has no printed date, so 2026-09-01 is an approximate source date. Federal Register queries on 'Yucca Mountain' and on DOE spent fuel documents found no DOE or NRC action to restart licensing, and the NRC's Yucca license application page (last reviewed 2026-09-14) does not state the status of the adjudication, so a quiet step is possible. The Mandate's call for a second repository by consent-based siting is partly mirrored by DOE's volunteer-state campuses, though DOE's pages describe fuel-cycle campuses rather than repositories; the stage is diverged because the Mandate's lead recommendation, restarting Yucca licensing, was not acted on and DOE is reported to be asking Congress to end the site's exclusive role.
